seo.h1: Buffalo Wild Wings Sauces, From Mild to Blazin'

question: What Sauces Does Buffalo Wild Wings Have?
quick_answer: Buffalo Wild Wings has about two dozen signature sauces and dry rubs, arranged on a heat scale from mild to extremely hot. Crowd favorites include Medium, Honey BBQ, Parmesan Garlic, Asian Zing, Mango Habanero and the Lemon Pepper and Desert Heat dry rubs. The hottest are the Blazin' sauces, which use Carolina Reaper peppers and are used in the Blazin' Challenge.
key_facts: About two dozen sauces and dry rubs, with limited-time flavors rotating in
Heat scale runs from mild to Blazin'
Dry rubs like Lemon Pepper and Desert Heat give flavor without the mess
Blazin' Knockout uses nine peppers, including Carolina Reaper and Devil's Breath
Blazin' Challenge: 10 Blazin' wings in 5 minutes, no water or napkins

body.heading: How the Buffalo Wild Wings heat scale works
body.text: Buffalo Wild Wings sorts its sauces and dry rubs on a heat scale that runs from mild at the bottom to Blazin' at the top. The menu shows where each flavor sits, so you can pick by heat level as well as by taste. The lineup is roughly two dozen flavors and changes as limited-time sauces come and go, so your local menu may show a few that aren't listed here.

body.heading: Mild and sweet sauces
body.text: If you don't want much heat, the safest picks are the sweet and savory sauces: Honey BBQ, Parmesan Garlic, Teriyaki and Orange Chicken, plus classic Mild buffalo, which is mostly butter and tang with a light kick. The Lemon Pepper and Salt & Vinegar dry rubs are also low on heat.

body.heading: Medium and sweet-heat sauces
body.text: The middle of the scale is where many regulars order. Medium is the classic buffalo wing flavor with more kick than Mild. Spicy Garlic adds garlic to buffalo heat, and Asian Zing and Caribbean Jerk bring sweet heat. Thai Curry, a coconut-curry sauce, is one of the most love-it-or-hate-it flavors on the menu. The Desert Heat dry rub adds smoky spice without sauce.

body.heading: Hot sauces
body.text: For real heat, the usual picks are Hot, Nashville Hot and Mango Habanero, which mixes fruity sweetness with habanero heat. Heat is personal, so some reviewers find certain mid-scale sauces hotter than expected. Above all of these are the Blazin' sauces at the very top of the scale.

body.heading: Blazin' sauces and the Blazin' Challenge
body.text: Blazin' sauces are the hottest at Buffalo Wild Wings. Blazin' Carolina Reaper is measured at more than two million Scoville units, and Blazin' Knockout is made with nine peppers, including Devil's Breath, Carolina Reaper, scorpion and ghost peppers. In the Blazin' Challenge, you try to eat 10 Blazin' wings in five minutes or less with no water or napkins. You must be 18 or older, sign a waiver and follow the official rules, which can change and are posted at participating restaurants and online.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a sauce and a dry rub?
faqs.a: Sauces coat the wings in a wet glaze. Dry rubs are seasoning blends, so the wings stay crispier and less messy.
